You manage an ML workflow for a fraud detection model. The source code for data processing and model training is stored in a version control repository. You need to implement a continuous training (CT) pipeline that automatically runs unit tests and launches a new training run on Agent Platform Pipelines when code is updated in the repository. You want to use a fully managed service to orchestrate this process. What should you do?

• Option A: Create a Cloud Run function that is triggered by repository commits. The function runs the unit tests, launches a custom training job, and uses Model Monitoring to validate the new model’s performance before deployment.
• Option B: Define a Cloud Workflow to monitor the repository for changes. Configure the workflow on Agent Platform Pipelines to orchestrate and run the unit tests. Use the model evaluation component to validate the new model’s performance before deployment.
• Option C: Configure Agent Platform Pipelines to poll the repository for updates. Add a conditional step in the pipeline that uses Model Monitoring to validate the new model’s performance before deployment.
✓ Option D: Create a Cloud Build trigger associated with the repository. Define a build configuration file that runs the unit tests and triggers a job on Agent Platform Pipelines. Use the model evaluation component to validate the model performance before deployment.
Final Key: D
✓ NB = Gemini = Vote (D)

Configure a Cloud Build trigger on the repository to run unit tests and submit the Vertex AI (Agent Platform) Pipeline, using the pipeline's model evaluation component to gate deployment.

📓 Grounded Source & Full Rationale
Source: Source #1 (PMLE June 2026 Exam Guide §5.2: CI/CD/CT with Cloud Build) & Source #2 (PMLE Study Guide v2.0 §5.2)
✅ Why D is Correct: Cloud Build is Google Cloud's native serverless CI/CD service that triggers automatically on Git commits to run unit tests and submit an Agent Platform Pipelines run, where the model evaluation component validates pre-deployment metrics on held-out test data. ❌ Why Others Fail: • A: Model Monitoring tracks post-deployment production drift/skew on live traffic and cannot validate an undeployed candidate model prior to deployment. • B: Cloud Workflows does not natively act as a CI test runner triggered by Git commits, nor should code unit tests be orchestrated inside ML pipeline runs. • C: Agent Platform Pipelines does not natively poll Git repositories for code commits, and Model Monitoring is a post-deployment tool rather than a pre-deployment gate.
  • × A Cloud Run functions are not a managed CI/CD test runner, and Model Monitoring is for post-deployment production drift rather than pre-deployment validation.
  • × B Cloud Workflows does not natively watch Git commits, and Vertex AI Pipelines is for ML steps rather than running source-code unit tests.
  • × C Vertex AI Pipelines does not poll Git repositories for commits, and Model Monitoring cannot evaluate an undeployed candidate model.

You are deploying a generative AI chatbot for an online gaming community using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. During beta testing, you discover that users are able to input malicious prompts that cause the model to generate hate speech and violent content. You need to implement a guardrail to block this content in production with minimal development overhead. What should you do?

• Option A: Update the system instruction (system prompt) of the model to explicitly state: “You are a helpful assistant. Do not generate hate speech or violent content.”
✓ Option B: Implement and configure Model Armor to sanitize responses if hateful content is detected.
• Option C: Create a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) job in Agent Platform, and tune the model using a curated dataset of safe, policy-compliant gaming conversations.
• Option D: Integrate the Cloud Natural Language API’s moderation capabilities to analyze and block toxic user prompts before they reach the chatbot model.
Final Key: B
✓ NB = Gemini = Vote (B)

Configure Model Armor on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform to automatically inspect prompts and sanitize or block responses containing hate speech and violent content.

📓 Grounded Source & Full Rationale
Source: Source #1 (PMLE June 2026 Exam Guide §6.1: Model Armor) & Source #5 (Google Cloud Model Armor Overview Docs)
✅ Why B is Correct: Model Armor is Google Cloud's managed GenAI guardrail service that screens prompts and sanitizes/blocks model responses against prompt injection, jailbreaks, hate speech, and violent/dangerous content via policy templates with minimal development overhead. ❌ Why Others Fail: • A: System prompt instructions ('Do not generate hate speech') are soft behavioral hints that adversarial jailbreak prompts routinely bypass. • C: Supervised fine-tuning requires substantial dataset curation and training effort and still cannot deterministically guarantee blocking against novel adversarial attacks. • D: Filtering only user inputs with the Cloud Natural Language API misses obfuscated jailbreaks whose harmful hate/violence emerges only in the LLM's generated output, and requires custom middleware code.
  • × A System prompt instructions ('Do not generate hate speech') are easily bypassed by adversarial jailbreaks and malicious prompt injections.
  • × C Supervised fine-tuning on safe conversations requires dataset curation and training overhead and still does not provide a deterministic runtime safety guardrail.
  • × D Writing custom middleware to call the Cloud Natural Language moderation API requires custom code integration and lacks Model Armor's prompt-injection and LLM guardrail features.
